S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized by a combination of positive symptoms (such as delusions and hallucinations), negative symptoms (such as diminished emotional expression, motivation, and social engagement), and cognitive deficits, with functional decline lasting at least six months and active-phase symptoms for at least one month. Onset typically occurs in late adolescence to early adulthood, often with a prodromal period of subtle social withdrawal, decline in functioning, and odd thinking before clear psychotic symptoms emerge. The course is usually relapsing and remitting or steadily progressive, and long-term disability is closely tied to the burden of negative and cognitive symptoms rather than the intensity of positive symptoms alone. It is distinguished from mood disorders with psychotic features by the persistence of psychotic symptoms outside of mood episodes and from brief or substance-induced psychoses by its duration, functional deterioration, and lack of full return to premorbid functioning.

patient.personality: Jorge is an energetic, community-oriented organizer who thrives on structured planning by day and spontaneous, socially vibrant activities like dancing and neighborhood projects by night.
patient.stressor: About two and a half years ago, Jorge was promoted into a grant-funded role that dramatically increased his caseload and required him to manage a new outreach program in a neighborhood with escalating violence and political tension. The pressure to secure renewal funding, long hours writing reports, and exposure to increasingly distressed clients chipped away at his usual enthusiasm, and colleagues noticed he became unusually withdrawn during meetings and stopped volunteering to speak at community events. Over the next two years, his work performance declined: deadlines were missed, he let once-favorite projects stall, and he began avoiding social gatherings he used to organize, which led to formal warnings from his supervisor and the loss of a major grant he had championed. When he started spending most evenings alone in his apartment, neglecting his beloved salsa nights and community gardens, and his family saw that he no longer seemed engaged or emotionally responsive in conversations, they persuaded him to see a psychiatrist because they felt he was "no longer himself" and could no longer manage his job responsibilities reliably.
patient.chief_complaint: I just don’t feel any drive or interest in things anymore, even the stuff I used to love, and it’s getting hard to function at work.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Over the last couple of years I’ve become convinced that the people tied to this grant and some folks in the neighborhood council are secretly tracking what I do and say—like when I’m writing reports at home I feel certain they’re reading my emails and rearranging my caseload on purpose to make me fail, even though my brother keeps telling me it doesn’t make sense and there’s no proof of it at all.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: These days it’s like someone pulled the plug on me—where I used to be the first to organize a block clean-up or drag everyone out dancing, now I just sit on my couch staring at the wall after work, barely talking to my family or coworkers, not feeling much of anything and unable to push myself to do even simple things like return a phone call or water the plants in the community garden I started.
